Router Fault Under Review
Government officials said Saturday a single router installed by
L3Harris Technologies Inc.
may have caused the outage, Reuters reported. Transportation Secretary
Sean Duffy
said the cause remains undetermined.
Duffy said Friday the contractor was switching lines from copper wire to fiber.
In a statement, L3Harris said it has completed more than 70% of that conversion and is supporting the FAA’s investigation.

Duffy said the new routers flooded others with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The routers being replaced are about 25 years old, Duffy said, and were due for replacement in 2006.
Rare Stoppage Disrupts Air Travel
The FAA issued the ground stop around 4 p.m. EST Friday. Duffy said it was lifted around 8:15 p.m. The agency’s last widespread stoppage lasted about
